title: ca65 4510 target rejects the native ORA (indirect),z form
body:
The unchanged pinned cc65 4510 opcode target now passes the file-layout boundary fixed for #716, but the next source instruction fails:

```asm
.setcpu "4510"
 ora ($07),z
```

ca65 V2.18 + ld65 V2.18 accept this and emit `1207`. Asm198x reports:

```text
asm198x: input.s:2: error: `ORA` has no (indirect),z form
```

The complete target is pinned at cc65 `e11fb5c39371046ebe25485f984f644c5a0d65d3`. Its native 564-byte output matches the upstream `4510-opcodes.ref`, SHA-256 `8a5fcde630e55dd49403f7c6ffed25d8786e65e3d0a2723531b7ca3e2c0509ec`. The clean full-target producer was `18be570`; its full record is retained in [4510-after-extents.json](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/blob/60babae495e4e37963a5bbec23068ae21ff71eb3/docs/plans/2026-10-16-next-project-boundaries/4510-after-extents.json). The full source stops at line 22 with the same form diagnostic.

This is an observed form-selection/encoding boundary, not an established explanation of its mechanism. Trace lexical `.setcpu "4510"`, operand classification and the neutral ISA forms before changing code. If an ISA-spec correction is needed, use the owning Isa198x repo and primary citations. Preserve existing 6502/65C02/4502 behavior and source/debug identity. Capture native mode/refusal controls, formatter and CLI regressions, then rerun the complete unchanged project and retain its next boundary or exact final-byte match. Do not promote the whole target from this one instruction.

Minimal control config:

```text
MEMORY { MAIN:start=$1000,size=$7000,file=%O; }
SEGMENTS { CODE:load=MAIN,type=ro; }
```

Measured commands and streams:

```json
[
  {
    "argv": [
      "/opt/homebrew/bin/ca65",
      "input.s",
      "-o",
      "input.o"
    ],
    "exit": 0,
    "stdout": "",
    "stderr": ""
  },
  {
    "argv": [
      "/opt/homebrew/bin/ld65",
      "-C",
      "input.cfg",
      "input.o",
      "-o",
      "native.bin"
    ],
    "exit": 0,
    "stdout": "",
    "stderr": ""
  },
  {
    "argv": [
      "/private/tmp/asm198x-next-boundaries-build/debug/asm198x",
      "--dialect",
      "ca65",
      "-C",
      "input.cfg",
      "input.s",
      "-o",
      "asm.bin"
    ],
    "exit": 1,
    "stdout": "",
    "stderr": "asm198x: input.s:2: error: `ORA` has no (indirect),z form\n"
  }
]
```

Related #618 and #640. No upstream build script was executed.

title: SjASMPlus numeric digit separators are read as character literals
body:
The unchanged pinned SpecNext Invaders target passes its original logical ASSERT after #717, then fails at `src/audio.asm:11`:

```asm
 or %111'00'00'0
 and %111'00'11'1
```

SjASMPlus 1.21.0 accepts this and emits `f6e0e6e7`. Asm198x reports `malformed character literal`. The shared Z80 numeric-token extent currently ends before the apostrophe, leaving a quote to the character-literal path. This is a numeric-separator boundary, separate from string escape decoding and shift arithmetic.

The complete project pin is `e3211ea8ad2e83aca4d07d70bd8e09b7b51a9a1d`. A fresh full native build emits the expected 33,280-byte NEX, SHA-256 `5fbed92a7d60dab47de8b22162c9227df051eaf67c26e85e618b24f6429dd07f`. The clean Asm producer was `0b3f63cd5d3c2881b998c3ac51017dd0f3eb369d`. [Complete captured result](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/blob/60babae495e4e37963a5bbec23068ae21ff71eb3/docs/plans/2026-10-16-next-project-boundaries/specnext-after-logical-expressions.json).

Establish native separator rules across numeric bases, adjacent operators and invalid placement before extending the SjASMPlus numeric lexer. Preserve character literals, quoted strings, `AF'`, DEFINE substitution, source locations and Pasmo isolation; do not remove apostrophes globally. Add native-byte/refusal, formatter and CLI output-preservation controls. Rerun the unchanged whole target and retain the next boundary or exact final NEX match; this one correction must not imply complete compatibility.

Minimal native evidence:

```json
{
  "argv": [
    "/usr/local/bin/sjasmplus",
    "--raw=native.bin",
    "input.asm"
  ],
  "exit": 0,
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "SjASMPlus Z80 Cross-Assembler v1.21.0 (https://github.com/z00m128/sjasmplus)\nPass 1 complete (0 errors)\nPass 2 complete (0 errors)\nPass 3 complete\nErrors: 0, warnings: 0, compiled: 3 lines, work time: 0.000 seconds\n",
  "hex": "f6e0e6e7"
}
```

Related #618 and #640. No upstream build script was executed.

title: Establish native controls for the newer cc65 CPU opcode targets
body:
The pinned 6502DTV and 65CE02 opcode sources cannot currently be qualified with the installed native arbiter `ca65 V2.18 - N/A`. Its actual invocations fail with `Invalid CPU: '6502dtv'` and `Invalid CPU: '65ce02'`.

The automated ecosystem audit records these as reference-control failures and does not run or judge Asm198x for them. Both projects pin cc65 commit `e11fb5c39371046ebe25485f984f644c5a0d65d3` and include the upstream source and expected raw-byte files.

Establish a reference-tool revision/version that accepts these exact pinned sources, review and record its executable identity, and update the relevant audit tooling deliberately. Do not change a global arbiter identity silently, use a moving upstream branch, drop the targets, or count failed controls as Asm incompatibilities. Run native assembly/linking and compare the final raw artifacts before interpreting the next Asm result. Related #618 and #640.

The Asm producer revision was `652114a082cad7b094201e3ad7966544bb676a92`; its development version string was 0.0.69. That exact source is retained at [`evidence/ecosystem-producer-2026-10-16`](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/tree/evidence/ecosystem-producer-2026-10-16). The 0.0.70 public package qualification is separate.
